The label the map gives Taiwan in 2000 BCE. It appears to be a variant spelling of Dapenkeng, Taiwan's first farming culture, though by this date archaeologists see that culture as replaced by later Neolithic groups with finer cord-marked and red pottery.

These farmers grew rice and millet and lived in larger villages. Around 2200 BCE some of them crossed to the northern Philippines, the first step of the Austronesian spread across the Pacific and Indian oceans. Their descendants are Taiwan's indigenous peoples.
